entries.verificationTarget: w200: attempted removal of R3TR TABL ZORV_MCP_T01 position 000024 from task GR2K923473 in request GR2K923472
entries.notes: A real call was made and failed. The tool located the entry and passed its own pre-checks, then reported CTS_CLEANUP_POSTCHECK_ENTRY_REMAINS, and the entry is still present when E071 is read for GR2K923473 (returnedCount 25 including the target row). The PUT to /sap/bc/adt/cts/transportrequests/<task> returned 2xx and changed nothing: the request body listed tm:abap_object directly under tm:request, while the entry belongs to the task container, and SAP resolves the object against the container it is named in. The HTTP status alone could not have revealed this, because the ADT client already rejects 4xx and 5xx. The payload was corrected on 2026-09-24 to nest the objects in tm:task whenever the caller names a task that differs from the request, and that correction was then tested against w200: the PUT still returned 2xx and the entry was still present in E071, so the nesting is not proven to work. Two structurally different payload shapes have now been tried and neither removed anything, while the native ADT removeobject action is absent from the bundled abap-adt-api client and this tool's own availability has always been reported as unknown because it requires successful native ADT removeobject support on the target system. The tool is therefore best read as a platform limitation of ECC 7.31 SP04 rather than an open code defect - and it fails safely, because its own post-check refuses to report success, so no caller can be misled into believing an entry was removed. The practical remedy is to remove the entry in SE09/SE10. Nothing was released and no SAP standard object was touched.

entries.notes: Real call observed. entries.verificationTarget: w200: object recording observed in CTS containers GR2K923487 and GR2K923473
entries.notes: Real calls observed. The operation completed and the requested object was read back from E071, and repeating the identical call created no additional row, so the operation is idempotent. This tool was unusable before this acceptance for two independent reasons, both fixed: it had no pre-change observation branch, and the helper's post-insert read-back selected four columns into a table typed as the full E071 structure, whose first field is MANDT (CLNT 3), so the SELECT raised DBIF_RSQL_INVALID_RSQL and dumped after the entry had already been recorded. One contract hazard remains and is not fixed: TRINT_OBJECTS_CHECK_AND_INSERT refuses to record an object that already belongs to another open transport and returns that order and task instead, so the tool can report status completed with insertedCount 1 while the object is not in the request that was asked for. The returned requestNumber and taskNumber carry SAP's own values rather than an echo of the input, which is how a caller can detect the difference.

entries.verificationTarget: w200 client 200, allowlisted customer table ZTPMC_BZWL through the finite fallback dialect, 2026-09-25
entries.notes: Real calls recorded on 0.50.15 against w200. The platform does not serve the native ADT preview endpoint (the known empty-HTML answer), so every call ran the finite fallback dialect over RFC_READ_TABLE: SELECT * FROM ZTPMC_BZWL returned data with querySource.method=rfc_read_table, nativeCode=SAP_DATA_QUERY_RESPONSE_INVALID and six real field definitions; SELECT COUNT(*) returned the exact aggregate {COUNT: 70} with aggregateColumns [{expression: 'COUNT(*)', column: 'COUNT'}]; SELECT WERKS, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY WERKS returned two groups, {WERKS: 8020, COUNT: 3} and {WERKS: 809P, COUNT: 67}, whose sum matches the ungrouped count; and the same COUNT(*) with maxRows=50 was refused with TABLE_QUERY_AGGREGATE_INCOMPLETE rather than reporting a count of the sample, which is the exact-or-refuse contract observed rather than asserted. Two limits found by the same session and recorded in the evidence file: the dialect path is only reached when maxRows <= 500 (src/tools.ts throws the platform's own error above that, and the tool description does not state the cap), and read_ddic_structure rejects tables with OBJECT_TYPE_MISMATCH, so a table's field list has to come from read_abap_table or from the query's own fieldMetadata. What this does not prove: the native preview path stays unavailable on this release, and only one allowlisted table (the customer scope table) was exercised, so the dialect is verified against that table's types, not against every allowlisted type.

entries.verificationTarget: read-only against w200: MEDRUCK (positive, with and without includeSource) and ZZZZ_NOT_A_FORM (negative)
entries.notes: Real reads observed on the deployed 2.8 helper. MEDRUCK returned 1479 form lines, 2 pages, 14 page windows, 10 windows, 31 paragraphs, 5 strings and 91 tabs with fingerprint 222b2664; includeSource added sourceStatus ok with 104 definition lines and fingerprint b803dbf8. ZZZZ_NOT_A_FORM was rejected with NOT_FOUND and touched no state. Two helper-side defects were found and fixed during this acceptance: the source-status field was declared LENGTH 12 while the literal NOT_REQUESTED is 13 characters, so the service rejected its own truncated status; and the ID_DEF read used the display language instead of the definition language from the text header (TDOSPRAS), which made includeSource return an empty source for delivered forms.
